sections.title: Social phrasal verbs
sections.content:
Phrasal verbs are essential for natural-sounding English:
• get along with — have a good relationship. She gets along well with all her classmates.
• look up to — admire and respect. Many young people look up to their teachers.
• put up with — tolerate something unpleasant. I can't put up with this noise any longer.
• run into — meet unexpectedly. I ran into an old school friend at the supermarket.
• let down — disappoint someone. He promised to help but then let me down.

sections.title: Work and study phrasal verbs
sections.content:
Phrasal verbs commonly used in professional and academic settings:
• carry out — perform or complete a task. The team carried out extensive research.
• come up with — think of an idea or plan. She came up with a brilliant solution.
• figure out — understand after thinking. I finally figured out how to solve the problem.
• set up — establish or create. They set up a new company last year.
• hand in — submit work. Students must hand in their essays by Friday.

sections.title: Life events phrasal verbs
sections.content:
Phrasal verbs for significant moments:
• bring up — raise a child, or mention a topic. She was brought up by her grandparents.
• settle down — begin a stable life. After travelling for years, he decided to settle down.
• take after — resemble a parent. She takes after her mother in many ways.
• pass away — die (euphemism). His grandfather passed away peacefully at 92.

exercises.question: 'I can't put up with the noise' means I can't:
exercises.explanation: Put up with means to tolerate or endure something unpleasant.

exercises.question: To 'come up with' an idea means to:
exercises.hint: The idea appears in your mind.
exercises.explanation: Come up with means to produce or think of an idea, plan, or suggestion.

exercises.question: If a child 'takes after' their parent, they:
exercises.explanation: Take after means to resemble a parent or relative in appearance or character.

exercises.question: To 'let someone down' means to:
exercises.explanation: Let down means to fail to support or help someone; to disappoint.

exercises.question: 'She was brought up by her grandparents' means they:
exercises.hint: They were responsible for her childhood.
exercises.explanation: Bring up means to raise and care for a child until they are grown up.

exercises.question: To 'carry out' research means to:
exercises.explanation: Carry out means to perform or complete a planned action or task.

exercises.question: To 'run into' someone means to:
exercises.explanation: Run into means to meet someone unexpectedly.

exercises.question: To 'look up to' someone means to:
exercises.explanation: Look up to means to admire and respect someone.
